author: GNiendorf
body:
#### PR description:

This PR speeds up T5 building, the stage that dominates LST in dense events, without changing physics.

A T5 is an inner T3 (MD0-MD1-MD2) and an outer T3 (MD2-MD3-MD4), whose segments are the outer LS1 (MD2-MD3) and the outer LS2 (MD3-MD4). The first dBeta cut depends only on the inner T3 and the outer LS1, the second only on the inner T3's first segment and the outer LS2; then come the remaining cuts (radii, chi2, DNN).

Before, the T5 stage was:
- `CountTripletConnections`: one block per inner module; for every (inner T3, outer T3) pair both dBeta cuts, loosened (the full selection in dense modules); counts per inner T3 and per MD, and dBeta pass bits for the first 32 outer T3s.
- `CreateEligibleModulesListForQuintuplets` (single block): per-module T5 capacity and offsets, and the T5-by-MD ranges in a loop over the MDs of every module.
- `CreateQuintuplets`: every pair again, the full selection on each candidate, the T5 stored in a build-time collection.
- `CompactModuleOffsetsKernel`, `FinalizeQuintuplets` (fits and embedding, written at the exact size), `SetCompactModuleIndices`, after a second host synchronization.

The problems: the full selection runs a second time per candidate; the first dBeta cut is evaluated per outer T3 although it depends only on the outer LS1; a dense module of a jet core is processed by a single block, while in sparse events most threads of a block have no pair to test; the single-block kernel loops over all MDs.

After:
- `FillLSonT3ByMD` (new): per MD, the segments starting there that carry triplets (the "LS on T3"): the outer LS1 candidates of the inner T3s ending at that MD, with no loop over outer T3s.
- `CountTripletConnections` (rewritten): tiles of 64 inner T3s, one block per tile. One thread per (inner T3, outer LS1) applies the outer LS1 cuts once; then one thread per candidate (inner T3, outer T3) applies the outer LS2 cuts, through a cache of the last decision per outer LS2, and the remaining cuts. Work spreads evenly over the threads whatever the density, with the same code on every backend. Each selected pair is counted per module and per MD and recorded in a pair list; if the list overflows, the kernel is re-run with a larger one.
- `CreateEligibleModulesListForQuintuplets`: per-module counts only.
- `SetQuintupletRangesByMD` (new): the T5-by-MD ranges, one thread per MD.
- `AddSelectedQuintuplets` (new, replaces `CreateQuintuplets` and `FinalizeQuintuplets`): writes the T5s directly from the pair list at their exact size, without re-running any cut or compacting. It is launched twice (pairs of dense modules first) to keep the previous T5 order in the modules that reach the T5 cap.
- Unchanged: `ExtendT5FromDupT5ByMD`, `RemoveDupQuintupletsAfterBuild`.

All buffers that change are transient (T5 stage only); the stored T5 collection is unchanged.

#### PR validation:

HLT timing, hltLST, ms per event; Phase-2 HLT menus on CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-10-27-2300, 1 thread, median of 2 rounds:

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| CPU menu, QCD (high-pT jets) | 3150 | 1020 |
| CPU menu, ttbar | 300 | 289 |
| GPU menu (NVIDIA L40), QCD | 497 | 87 |
| GPU menu (NVIDIA L40), ttbar | 3.02 | 2.61 |

Physics: MTV, HLT and offline, 500 ttbar + 500 QCD PU200 events: efficiency, fake and duplicate rates unchanged. Plots: HLT [ttbar](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/hlt_ttbar/plots_hlt.html), [QCD](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/hlt_qcd/plots_hlt.html); offline [ttbar](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/off01_ttbar/index.html), [QCD](https://gniendorf.github.io/lst-plots/internal-prs/lst-t5-enumeration/off01_qcd/index.html)
title: LST T5: leverage on individual outer LS1 and LS2 segment cut passing
